53-L01.title: Accountant
53-L01.description: Individuals qualify as certified public accountants (CPA) . To be eligible to be a CPA, an individual must pass the CPA exam and have completed at least 150 semester credits of college education, including: A B.A.e degree or higher 24 semester credits in accounting subjects with 15 credits at the upper or graduate level and 24 semester credits in business administration subjects.

53-L24.title: Certified Public Accountant
53-L24.description: Individuals must have a B.A., 24 semester credits in accounting, with 15 credits at the upper or graduate level, 24 semester credits in business administration, take and pass the uniform cerfified public accountant (CPA) exam, and have a minimum of 12 months/2,000 hours of accounting work using the skills generally used in business and accounting and auditing, verified by a licensed CPA.

00-78.title: Enrolled Actuary
00-78.description: Enrolled Actuaries meet experience requirements and pass an examination. EAs are experts on the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The EA designation is awarded by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries, located at the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. Renewal every 3 years requires continuing actuarial education and other professional development activities. For detailed information, see http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-utl/20cfr901.pdf or http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/actuaries/index.html.
00-78.agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury · Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries

53-L49.title: Engineer
53-L49.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay $65 fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L10.title: Agricultural Engineer
53-L10.description: Individuals must have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, pass the engineer-in-training examination and Principles and Practices of Engineering examination for the agricultural branch, complete the required application and pay the required fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The FAA Advisory Circular, AC 61-12M, Student Pilot Guide, outlines general procedures for obtaining student and private pilot certificates. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.102-61.117, and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-60.title: Medical Doctor
00-60.description: A ship's Medical Doctor is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A medical doctor must also hold a valid license as a physician or surgeon issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-60.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

53-L39.title: Doctor
53-L39.description: Individuals must have graduated from an accredited or approved medical school, completed a residency or other post-graduate training program, provide a work history, provide a list of hospital privileges, have a state medical license, provide required information, pay required fees.

53-L105.title: Osteopathic Physician
53-L105.description: Individuals must have graduated from an accredited or approved osteopathic school, completed an examination approved by the National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners, have completed at least one year of post-graduate training, must provide a work history for the time subsequent to receipt of osteopathic degree. Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L12.title: Animal Massage
53-L12.description: Individuals must successfully complete a 300-hour approved training program, successfully complete a qualifying examination and fill out the required application form.

53-L15.title: Architect
53-L15.description: Individuals must have an accredited B.A. or master's degree in architecture, or take an examination they do not have the required degree. Individuals must also complete the requried application and pay the required $75 fee

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-48.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-38.title: Second Mate - Upper Level
00-38.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Mate Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on ocean steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Third Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-38.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

53-L20.title: Boxer (Professional)
53-L20.description: Individuals must be 18 years old, complete the required license application, provide evidence of the completed physical examination (signed by the doctor) and pay the required fee of $25.

53-L63.title: Inspector (Boxing, Wrestling, Martial Arts)
53-L63.description: Individuals must submit a completed combative sports license application, completed combative sports certification of completed hours and pay required $65 fee.

53-L69.title: Judge (Boxing, Wrestling, Martial Arts)
53-L69.description: Invidividuals must send a completed combative sports license application, and pay the required $65 fee.

53-L70.title: Kick Boxer (Professional)
53-L70.description: Invidividuals must send a completed combative sports license application, have a physical examinations, and and pay the required $25 fee.

53-L77.title: Magager (Boxing, Wrestling, Martial Arts)
53-L77.description: Invidividuals must send a completed combative sports license application and and pay the required $65 fee.

53-L114.title: Physican (Boxing, Wrestling, Martial Arts)
53-L114.description: Individuals must be at least 18 years old, must complete a combative sports license application and pay the required fee.

53-L127.title: Referees (Boxing, Wrestling, Martial Arts)
53-L127.description: Individuals must complete a combative sports license application, complete a Combative Sports Certification of Official form, proof of a physical examination for referees and pay the required $65 fee.

53-L150.title: Athletic trainer
53-L150.description: Evaluate and advise individuals to assist recovery from or avoid athletic-related injuries or illnesses, or maintain peak physical fitness. May provide first aid or emergency care.

53-L17.title: Athletic Trainer
53-L17.description: Individuals must have a B.A. and provide a transcript, pass a requried athletic trainers' examination, provide required personal information, and have graduated from a Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education-accredited athletic training program.

53-L151.title: Audiologist
53-L151.description: Assess and treat persons with hearing and related disorders. May fit hearing aids and provide auditory training. May perform research related to hearing problems.

53-L19.title: Audiologist
53-L19.description: Individuals must have a B.A. and provide a transcript, have a minimum o f 36 weeks of full-time post-graduate professional experience or equivalent, pass the nationally-recognized audiology examination or receive competency certification from a major audiology and hearing professional organization, verify that they are covered by a surety bond, provide required personal information.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

00-65.title: Ship Radar Endorsement
00-65.description: The Ship Radar Endorsement is issued by the Federal Communications Commission to licensed commercial radio operators. This endorsement allows them to repair, maintain, or internally adjust ship radar equipment. Passing a written exam is required. For further information, see the FCC web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/sre.html.

53-L32.title: Cosmetologist
53-L32.description: Individuals must graduate from licensed and approved costetology school of at least 1,600 hours or successfully complete a state-approved apprenticeship training program of at least 2,000 hours in cosmetology, pass the state-approved written and performance examinations, and pay the required $25 licensing fee.

53-L65.title: Instructor (Cosmetology)
53-L65.description: Individuals must have graduated from an approved an licensed school with the requried 500 classroom hours, pass the state-approved written and performance examiniations and pay the required $25 fee.

53-L108.title: Permanent Cosmetics Artist
53-L108.description: Individuals must be at least 18 years old, have a current bloodborne pathgens certificate, complete and submit a Body Art, Body Piercing, Tatoo Artist, Permanent Cosmetics License, Renewal or Reinstatement application and pay required $250 fee.

53-L175.title: Drug Controlled Substance Researcher Registration
53-L175.description: Registration RequirementsChapter 69.50 RCWChapter 246-887 WACRequirementsApplicants for a controlled substance researcher must list the controlled substances to be used, the purpose for such use, and the names of the people authorized to access the controlled substances. The applicant must develop policies and procedures for the storage, security, accountability, as well as recordkeeping for the acquisition and disposition of the controlled substances. 00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

53-L11.title: Amusement Ride Inspector
53-L11.description: Individuals must have two years of experience as an amusement ride inspector, personnel supervision responsibility for erecting, maintaining and operating functions. Individuals must also pass a competency examination administered by the National Association of Amusement Ride Safety Officials, pay a $20 feel to the department, and documentation of having met the above requirements. Trainees may work without certification, if directly and continually supervised during the inspection process by a certified ride inspector.

53-L60.title: Home Inspector
53-L60.description: Individuals must take an approved 120-hour Fundamentals of Home Inspection course and mentor with an experienced home inspector for 40 hours of field training, submit home inspector examination application and take the examination ($300 fee), and pay the $680 licensing fee.

53-L64.title: Inspector of Solid Waste Incinerator and Landfill Facilities
53-L64.description: Individuals must pass have a high school diploma or equivalent, Solid Waste Association of North America's examination (cost $210), and (for prospective landfill facilities inspectors) have a minimum of 2 years of experience as a landfill inspector.

53-L99.title: On-site Designer And Inspector
53-L99.description: Individuals must have a high school diploma or GED, at least 4 years of approved experience showing increased responsibility for the desigh of on-site waste-ater treatment systems, a passing score on the written On-site Designer License examination, a passing score on the Law and Ethics examination, submitting a completed application and paying the required fee.

53-L109.title: Pest Inspector
53-L109.description: Individuals must pass the structural pest inspector examination, take the Laws and Safety examination and take category examinations in the areas individual is to work in, submit proof of financial coverage or be employed by a state Department of Agriculture-approved structural pest inspector company, own or be employed by a business that has a structural pest inspector company license.

53-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
53-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.

53-L152.title: Cardiovascular invasive specialist
53-L152.description: Conduct tests on pulmonary or cardiovascular systems of patients for diagnostic purposes. May conduct or assist in electrocardiograms, cardiac catheterizations, pulmonary functions, lung capacity, and similar tests. Includes vascular technologists.

53-L26.title: Chemical Engineer
53-L26.description: Individuials must pass the engineer-in-training and the principles and practices of engineering examiniation for the chemical branch, have 8 years of 8 years of professional experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, pay required fee.

requirements.label: Exam

53-L146.title: Administrative staff
53-L146.description: Staff employed in Principal, Vice-Principal, Superintendent, Director, and other roles
53-L146.agency: Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction

53-L27.title: Chiropractor
53-L27.description: Individuals must have graduated from an accredited chiropractic college and show evidence of at least 4,000 classroom hours of instruction, completion of at least one-half of B.A. requirements at an accredited college, successful completion of the National Board of Chiropractic Examiners Test Parts 1-IV, work history chonology and answers to personal data questions.

53-L28.title: Civil Engineer
53-L28.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the civil branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay required fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L135.title: Structural Engineer
53-L135.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the structural branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L03.title: Adjuster (Insurance)
53-L03.description: Individuals must have completed the required 20 hours of coursework for each line of insurance to be involved in, taken and passed the required examination, be 18, and be fingerprinted.

53-L07.title: Agent (Insurance)
53-L07.description: Insurance agents solicit, negoitiation and/or sell insurance contracts. They are licensed by line of insurance and activity and are licensed as "producers".

53-L88.title: Mining Engineer
53-L88.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the mining branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L34.title: Court Reporter
53-L34.description: Individuals must pass the state court reporter examination, fill out the required application and pay the required fee.

53-L36.title: Dentist
53-L36.description: Individuals must have graduated from a dental school approved by the Dental Quality Assurance Commission, successfully completed the National Board Dental Examination, and clinical examination, provide a work history, have a state licensen and pay the required fees.

53-L38.title: Dietitian
53-L38.description: Individuals must have a BA or higher in nutrition, foods and nutrition, dietetics or food management, provide evidence of completion of preprofessional experience or coordinated undergraduate program, pass the written examnation, have a state license, provide required information and pay the required fee.

53-L96.title: Nutritionist
53-L96.description: Individual must have a B.A. or higher in major course of study in human nutrition, dietetics or food management, eveidence of completion of preprofessional experience or coordinated undergraduated program in dietetics under supervision of a qualified supervisor, pass a written examination. Masters degree in nutrition may substitute for preprofessional experience and written examination. Individual must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individual must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L42.title: Electrical Engineer
53-L42.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the electrical branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L04.title: Administrator (Electrical)
53-L04.description: Individuals must take and pass the administrator examination, pay the required fee and fill out the required form.

53-L43.title: Electrician
53-L43.description: Individuals must have completed 24 hours of basic classroom instruction for general journey level and 48 hours more for specialties requiring 4,000 hours of experience or 24 hours more for specialties requiring 2,000 hours of experience, have 8,000 documented hours working as an electrical trainee under the supervision of a certified electrician or equivalent military experience, fill out required application and pay required fee.

53-L44.title: Elevator Mechanic
53-L44.description: Individuals must have a minimum of three years of documented work experience, have college or trade school course work or equivalent, such as national elevator training programs or company training programs, fill out application, pay fee.

53-L82.title: Mechanic (Elevator)
53-L82.description: Individuals must either be nationally certified under the National Elevator Industry Education Program or the Certified Elevator Technician Program sponsored by the National Association of Elevator Contractors, or have earned a certificate of completion of an elevator mechanic apprenticeship program that met required standards and is registered with the Washington State Apprenticeship and Training Council or by completing a written examination and provide proof of documented experience and education creduts in the elevator industry performing conveyance work as verified by current and prior employers AND fill out the required application and pay the required $164.10 fee.

53-L45.title: Embalmer
53-L45.description: Individuals must be at least 18 years old, must have an A.A. degree in mortuary science (or have at least 5 years active licensed experience in another state, complete an embalmer internship, pass the licensing examination and pay the required $300 fee.

53-L46.title: Emergency Medical Service Evaluator
53-L46.description: Individuals must have an Department of Health provider credential, association with a licensed EMS agency and supervision of the county medical program director. Required education includes taking an approved EMS evaluatior curriculum, passing the evaluator examination and paying the required fee.

53-L47.title: Emergency Medical Service Personnel
53-L47.description: Individuals must have an Department of Health provider credential, association with a licensed EMS agency and supervision of the county medical program director. Required education includes taking an approved EMS curriculum, passing the EMS examination and paying the required fee.

53-L48.title: Emergency Medical Technician
53-L48.description: Individuals must have an Department of Health provider credential, association with a licensed EMS agency and supervision of the county medical program director. Required education includes taking an approved EMS evaluatior curriculum and passing the evaluator examination, pass a written examination and pay the required fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L107.title: Paramedic
53-L107.description: Individuals must have a high school diploma or GED, must complete Approved Paramedic Training Course, must be associated with a licensed EMS agency, a law enforcement agency, a business with an organized industrial safety team or be senior EMS instructors or coordinators. Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L50.title: Environmental Engineer
53-L50.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the environmental branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

requirements.label: Exam

53-L52.title: Esthetician
53-L52.description: Individuals must graduate from licensed and approved costetology school of at least 1,600 hours or successfully complete a state-approved apprenticeship training program of at least 2,000 hours in cosmetology, passs the state-approved written and performance examinations, and pay the required $25 licensing fee.

53-L126.title: Recreational Therapist
53-L126.description: Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L54.title: Financial Planner
53-L54.description: Individuals must register in the Investment Advisor Registration Depository operated by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). Registering in Washington costs $40 as a representative of a firm, or $150 as a sole proprietor. Invididuals must pass qualifying examinations, file a financial statement and file a proposed client contract.

53-L68.title: Investment Advisor
53-L68.description: Individuals must register in the Investment Advisor Registration Depository operated by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). Registering in Washington costs $40 as a representative of a firm, or $150 as a sole proprietor. Invididuals must pass qualifying examinations, file a financial statement and file a proposed client contract.

00-FinOpL.title: Series 39 - Direct Participation Programs Limited Principal
00-FinOpL.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over sales of: ?Direct participation program limited partnerships (e.g., real estate, oil and gas, and equipment leasing) ?Limited liability companies ?S corporations In addition to sales supervision, the Series 39 qualifies a principal for the overall supervision of a firm’s investment banking and securities business—including compliance, underwriting and advertising—for those activities specially covered by each supervisory principal’s license.

53-L29.title: Clandestine Drug Lab Cleanup Worker, Supervisor
53-L29.description: Individuals must complete 40-hour hazardous wast operations training, enroll in a 2-day clandestine drug lab worker certification course, submit application and pay initial $100 fee or $50 renewal fee. Supervisors must become certified workers, complete a 1-day clandestine drug lab decontamination supervisor certification course, submit an application and pay $200 initial or $150 renewal fee.

53-L41.title: Drug Lab Cleanup Worker, Supervisor
53-L41.description: Individuals must complete 40 hour Hazardous Waste Operations training, complete 2-day clandestine drug lab worker certification course, submit application and pay required fee. Supervisors must also take an additional certification course and submit application and pay required fee.

53-L160.title: Funeral Director
53-L160.description: Perform various tasks to arrange and direct funeral services, such as coordinating transportation of body to mortuary, interviewing family or other authorized person to arrange details, selecting pallbearers, aiding with the selection of officials for religious rites, and providing transportation for mourners.

53-L90.title: Mortician
53-L90.description: Individuals must be at least 18 years old, have an Associate of Arts (A.A.) degree in mortuary science (or meet alternative education requirements or have at least 5 years active licensed experience in another state), pass the required examination ($100 fee), complete Funeral Director license application and pay the required fee.

53-L56.title: Geologist
53-L56.description: Individuals must graduate from an accredited college or university with a degree in geological sciencess and have at least 5 years of documented and verifiable professional geological practice (or specialty practice if applying for a specialty), must be of good moral and ethical character (as assested to by 2 references) and pass the National Association of State Boards of Geology examination.

53-L87.title: Midwife
53-L87.description: Individuals must have graduated from an approved midwifery program, must have successfully passed both the national an state Midwifery Licensure examinations, have two letters of recommendation, must provide a work history from receipt of midwifery degree, have 7 hours of HIV/AIDS training, provided information about physical and mental health status, verifying lack of impairment due to chemical dependency/substance abuse, any history of loss of licensure or certification, loss or limitations of privileges, disciplinary actions as well as professional liability claims history.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

53-L94.title: Nursing Assistant
53-L94.description: Individuals must have a minimum of 85 hours of training through a state approved program, must pass the state competency examination, list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history, file an application and pay required fee.

53-L95.title: Nursing Home Administrator
53-L95.description: Individuals must have a BA from a recognized institution, must provide professional experience in the health care and management field, provide proposed administrator-in-training program, including proposed rotation hours through nursing home departments and a written proposal for a problem solving project. This program must be at least 1,500 hours. Individual must pass NAB examination. Individual must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individual must file application and pay required fee. Individual must renew license every year.

53-L169.description: Duties of nursing pool—Application of uniform disciplinary act—Criminal background checks.(1) The nursing pool shall document that each temporary employee or referred independent contractor provided or referred to health care facilities currently meets the applicable minimum state credentialing requirements.(2) The nursing pool shall not require, as a condition of employment or referral, that employees or independent contractors of the nursing pool recruit new employees or independent contractors for the nursing pool from among the permanent employees of the health care facility to which the nursing pool employee or independent contractor has been assigned or referred.(3) The nursing pool shall carry professional and general liability insurance to insure against any loss or damage occurring, whether professional or otherwise, as the result of the negligence of its employees, agents or independent contractors for acts committed in the course of their employment with the nursing pool: PROVIDED, That a nursin...

53-L149.title: Hearing aid specialist
53-L149.description: Select and fit hearing aids for customers. Administer and interpret tests of hearing. Assess hearing instrument efficacy. Take ear impressions and prepare, design, and modify ear molds.

53-L158.title: Speech-Language Pathology Assistant
53-L158.description: Assist speech-language pathologists in the assessment and treatment of speech, language, voice, and fluency disorders. Implement speech and language programs or activities as planned and directed by speech-language pathologists.

53-L59.title: Home Care Aide
53-L59.description: Individuals must successfully complete 75 hours of training through a program approved by the Washington State Department of Social and Health Services, successfully pass the home care aide examination and have a successful background check.

53-L62.title: Industrial Engineer
53-L62.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the industrial branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

53-L22.description: Individuals must have completed the required 20 hours of coursework for each line of insurance to be involved in, taken and passed the required examination, be 18, and be fingerprinted.

53-L75.title: Life Settlements Broker (Insurance)
53-L75.description: Individuals must have completed the required 20 hours of coursework for each line of insurance to be involved in, taken and passed the required examination, be 18, be fingerprinted and pay the required $100 fee (in addition to required $60 fee for a life insurance producer broker).

53-L137.title: Surplus Line Broker (Insurance)
53-L137.description: Individuals must have completed the required 20 hours of coursework for each line of insurance to be involved in, taken and passed the required examination, be 18, and be fingerprinted.

53-L122.title: Psychologist
53-L122.description: Invididuals must have completed a doctoral degree in psychology from a regionally accredited instituttion, must have one year or 750 hours in residency and a 300 hour practicum, must be able to verify a total of 3,300 hours of supvervision (including pre-internship, intership and post-doctoral supervised experience). Individuals must provide a work history for the time subsequent to receipt of degree. Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L72.title: Landscape Architect
53-L72.description: Individuals must successfully pass the Landscape Architect Registration Examination of the Council of Landscape Architectural Registration Boards, complete the landscape architecture licensure application, provide a written law review related to the practice of landscape architecture, and pay the required fees of $225 for the license application and $360 for the license.

53-L18.title: Attorney
53-L18.description: Individuals must pass the state bar examination and meet annual continuing legal education requirements.

53-L73.title: Lawyer
53-L73.description: Individuals must pass the state bar examination, pay the $355 in required fees and meet annual continuing legal education requirements.

53-L51.description: Individuals must pass the licensing test and pay the required fee.

53-L76.title: Loan Originator
53-L76.description: Individuals must pass the national and state mortgage loan originator tests (at a cost of $143 for both), have a high school diploma or equivalent, complete 22 hours of NMLS-approved pre-licensing education, including 4 hours in Washington law, complete a criminal background check and file a credit report authorization.

53-L89.title: Mortgage Broker
53-L89.description: Individuals must be at least 18 years old, must have a high school diploma or equivalent, have successfully completed 90 hours of approved real estate education, and passed the broker's examination.

53-L74.title: Licensed Practical Nurse
53-L74.description: Individuals must pass the licensed practical nurse examination and pay the required $92 fee.

53-L119.title: Practical Nurse
53-L119.description: Individuals must have successfully graduated from an accredited and approved nursing program, submit required application and pay required $92 fee.

53-L78.title: Manicurist
53-L78.description: Individuals must be at least 17 years old, graduate from licensed and approved costetology school of at least 600 hours or successfully complete a state-approved apprenticeship training program of at least 800 hours, pass the state-approved written and performance examinations, and pay the required licensing fee.

53-L133.title: Ship Design Engineer
53-L133.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the ship design branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

53-L33.title: Counselor
53-L33.description: Individuals must have a B.A in a counseling-related field, pass the state Certified Counselor examination, have a written supervisory agreement, fill out the required form, and pay the required fee.

53-L53.title: Family Therapist
53-L53.description: Individuals must have a master's or doctoral degree in marriage and family therapy from an approved school. Individuals must have a minimum of 2 calendar years of full-time marriage and family therapy, 1,000 hours of which must be direct client contact. Individuals must pass the Association of Marital and Family Therapy Regulatory Boards and pay the required fee.

53-L80.title: Marriage Therapist
53-L80.description: Individuals must have a master's or doctoral degree in marriage and family therapy from an approved school. Individuals must have a minimum of 2 calendar years of full-time marriage and family therapy, 1,000 hours of which must be direct client contact. Individuals must pass the Association of Marital and Family Therapy Regulatory Boards and pay the required fee.

53-L81.title: Massage Practitioner
53-L81.description: Individuals must have completed a Washington State Board of Massage-approved education programand have successfully passed the national examination offered by either the National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage and Bodywork or the Federation of State Massage Therapy Boards, answer statements about physical and mental health status, criminal background, any disciplinary actions, liability claims history, certify a lack of impairment due to chemical dependency/substance abuse and pay the required fee.

53-L86.title: Metallurgical Engineer
53-L86.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the metallurgical branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

53-L83.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the mechanical branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

53-L58.title: Health Care Assistant (Now Medical Assistant)
53-L58.description: Individuals must successfully complete high school or equivalent, read, write and converse in English, successfully complete college or post-secondary program accredited by the Accrediting Bureau of Health Education Schools or the Commission or Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (or listed equivalent), successfully passed the certified medical assistant examination through the American Association of Medical Assistants OR the registered medical assistant cerfication through the American Medical Technologists OR the clinical medical assistant certification examination through the National Health Career Association or the certified medical assistant examination through the National Center for Competency Testing.

53-L156.title: Respiratory care practitioner
53-L156.description: Assess, treat, and care for patients with breathing disorders. Assume primary responsibility for all respiratory care modalities, including the supervision of respiratory therapy technicians. Initiate and conduct therapeutic procedures; maintain patient records; and select, assemble, check, and operate equipment.

53-L130.title: Respiratory Therapist
53-L130.description: Individuals must have graduated from accredited 2-year respiratory therapy educational program, must pass the National Board for Respiratory Care entry-level examination and must have either met the eduucational criteria to sit for the advanced practicioner examinations or have been issued the respiratory therapist credential by the board. Individuals must provide a work history for the time subsequent to receipt of osteopathic degree. Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L92.title: Nuclear Engineer
53-L92.description: Individuals must pass the engineer-in-training examination, pass the principles and practices of engineering examination for the nuclear branch, have 8 years of professional-level experience under the direct supervision of a licensed engineer, send in a completed application and pay the required fee.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

53-L06.title: Advanced Registered Nurse Practitioner
53-L06.description: Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (ARNPs) are independent in their scope of medical practice including full prescription authority. They must pass the required examiniation, pay the required fee and fill out the required form.

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

53-L170.title: Nursing Technician
53-L170.description: A nursing technician (NTEC) is a nursing student preparing for RN licensure who meets the qualifications for licensure under RCW 18.79.340.

53-L97.title: Occupational Therapist
53-L97.description: Individual must have graduated from a nationally accredited, board certified school, have a minimum of 6 months of supervised fieldwork experience, must provide a work history dating from graduation of occupational therapy school. Individual must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L100.title: Operator of Solid Waste Incinerator and Landfill Facilities
53-L100.description: Individuals must pass an operator training course and a written examination. Incinerator certifications cost $200 for certification, $50 application fee, $160 textbook costs. Landfill operators must have a high school diploma or GED, must pass the required examination, must have 5 years of MSW management experience and 2 years of operating experience. Certifications last for 3 years. Required courses are taught by the Solid Waste Associaion of North American using private instructors under a memorandum of understanding with the state Department of Ecology.

53-L98.title: Ocularist
53-L98.description: Individual must have graduated from high school or completed a GED, be at least 18 years old, have competed either an apprenticeship program in Washington or have at least 5 years of out-of-state experience or have completed a prescribed approved ocularist course. Individual must have successfully completed state-administered examination. Individual must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individual must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L101.title: Optician
53-L101.description: Individuals must be at least 18 years old, a graduate of an accredited high school or with a GED, be of good moral character, have completed at least 3 years of apprenticeship training or have sucessfully completed a prescribed course in opticianry in an approved college or university or have been a dispensing optician in another state for 5 years, must submit required application and pay a $200 fee for the required examination.

53-L102.title: Optometrist
53-L102.description: Individuals must have graduated from an accredited school of optometry approved by the Washington State Board of Optometry, successfully completed the National Board of Examiners in Optometry Parts I-III and the Treatment and Management of Ocular Disease and have endorsements for DPA/TPA, oral medications and epinephrine by injection. Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L103.title: Orthopedic
53-L103.description: Individuals must have graduated from an accredited or approved medical school, completed a residency or other post-graduate training program, provide a work history, provide a list of hospital privileges, have a state medical license, provide required information, pay required fees.

53-L104.title: Orthotist
53-L104.description: Individuals must be 18 years old, have a B.A. or certificate program from an approved school, completed a clinical internship or residency of 1,900 hours, completed multiple choice and patient simulation examinations administered by the American Board for Certification in Orthotics and Prosthetices. Individuals must list states where credentials were granted and were applied for, provide information on physical and mental health, lack of impairment due to chemical dependency, any felony convictions or loss or limitations of privileges, any disciplinary actions and a professional liability claims history. Individuals must submit application and pay required fee.

53-L121.title: Prosthetist
53-L121.description: Individuals must be 18 years old, have a B.A. or certificate program from an approved school, completed a clinical internship or residency of 1,900 hours, completed multiple choice and patient simulation examinations administered by the American Board for Certification in Orthotics and Prosthetices. 53-L116.title: Physician Assistant (Osteopathic)
53-L116.description: Individuals must have graduated from an accredited or approved physician assistant program, passed an examination approved by the National Commissionon Certification of Physician Assistants, must provide a list of all work from the receipt of osetopathic degree. 00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.

53-L117.title: Plumber
53-L117.description: Individuals must pass the required Plumber Certification examination, submit the required application and pay the required $151.90 fee. 00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-04.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.

00-37.title: Chief Mate - Upper Level
00-37.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Mate - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on Any Gross Tons oceangoing steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Second Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

00-34.title: Deck Officers
00-34.description: The navigation of a vessel and management of the deck department is the responsibility of the Deck Officers. Deck officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Master, Chief Mate, Second Mate, Third Mate, Mate and Operator), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam, Motor, Sail or Auxiliary Sail), vessel tonnage (from not more than 5 to any gross register tons), and route (e.g., Inland, Great Lakes, Near Coastal or Oceans). Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

00-40.title: Master - Lower Level
00-40.description: Obtaining a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Lower Level requires a specified amount of qualifying service based on details such as vessel size and area of operation (ocean, near coastal, Great Lakes, or inland). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
